description:
pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs:256-266 — RsaMinKeySizeLint uses rsa_modulus_byte_len which calls der_tlv_value_len. The DER INTEGER for an unsigned value includes a leading 0x00 byte when the high bit would otherwise be set. For a true 2048-bit key, the DER INTEGER value is 257 bytes (256 magnitude + 1 leading zero). The check `n_bytes >= 256` accepts 256+ bytes, so a 2047-bit key (256 bytes, no leading zero needed) passes.

The doc comment acknowledges: 'n_bytes >= 256 accepts both 2048-bit keys (257 bytes) and 2047-bit keys (256 bytes). This is the same floor-byte comparison used by most CA/B Forum linting tools and matches zlint's behavior.'

However, the doc comment also claims 'DER INTEGER encoding of unsigned values: a leading 0x00 byte is prepended when the high bit of the first content byte would be 1.' This description is for UintRef (sign-stripped) but der_tlv_value_len gets the raw INTEGER VALUE length, which DOES include the leading zero. For a 2048-bit key: high bit set → DER prepends 0x00 → total value length = 257 bytes → 257 >= 256 → Pass.

BUT the description on lines 211-213 says 'der_tlv_value_len returns ... the byte length of the modulus INTEGER value (including any leading 0x00 byte).' This is correct, the check >= 256 is therefore accepting 2047-bit keys as passing (256 bytes without leading zero = bit length ~2047).

The comment at line 213-214 says: 'Therefore n_bytes >= 256 accepts both 2048-bit keys (257 bytes) and 2047-bit keys (256 bytes). This is the same floor-byte comparison used by most CA/B Forum linting tools and matches zlint's behavior.'

The CA/B Forum TLS BR §6.1.5 actually requires >= 2048 bits. Accepting 2047-bit keys is a protocol relaxation. This may be intentional to match industry practice, but it contradicts the strict spec reading.

P3 — minor spec deviation from TLS BR §6.1.5, intentionally matches zlint.
title: RsaMinKeySizeLint uses raw INTEGER byte length including leading 0x00 padding byte
